features.name: Secrets never block a publish

features.evidence: src/commands/create.ts reports secret-pattern findings in the files that would be pushed and publishes anyway; credential files are still unstaged from the commit so they are never published; a credential file already in git history now produces a warning instead of a block; --allow-secrets is accepted as a no-op so older scripts keep working; 3 new tests in test/create.test.ts cover the publish-with-a-secret, the credential exclusion, and the history warning

features.name: Picker presentation
features.description: Skill list shows names only; each row shows an empty box that becomes a green tick when ticked
features.evidence: src/commands/pick-skills.ts builds on @clack/core's MultiSelectPrompt for the keyboard handling and draws the list itself, because clack hardcodes its checkbox symbols; every box starts empty (initialValues is empty) and the header shows the running count; verified in a pty that an unticked row renders a dim empty box (ESC[2m), a ticked row a green tick (ESC[32m), that descriptions are gone, that the list scrolls in a short terminal, and that confirming with nothing ticked exits 1 without publishing

features.name: Install scope
features.description: kitcrate add asks whether to install into the project or the user's home, records the choice in kitcrate-lock.json, and install/update/remove act on it
features.evidence: src/core/scope.ts (InstallScope, DEFAULT_SCOPE, scopeDirectory); CollectionLockEntrySchema.scope defaults to 'project' so pre-change lockfiles still load; add prompts with clack select on a TTY, takes global from --global, and defaults to project under --yes/--json/non-TTY; install/update/remove pass entry.scope to the skills API; removeCollectionSkills takes a scope. Verified in a pty: the prompt renders both options and a cancelled prompt prints 'Cancelled.' with exit 130; a real global add put the skill in $HOME/.agents/skills and a project add in <project>/.agents/skills. test/add.test.ts covers both scopes plus remove and install round trips; test/lockfile.test.ts covers the backwards-compatible default and a global round trip. Preexisting detection is filtered to the chosen scope, so adding globally after the same collection was added to the project installs it in both places instead of skipping every member as preexisting; test/add.test.ts proves it, and removing the filter makes only that test fail.

features.name: Publish into a repository that already has remotes
features.description: kitcrate create chooses a free remote name instead of letting gh default to origin, and a failed publish can be retried
features.evidence: src/core/remote.ts holds the policy as a pure function (origin when free, github when origin is taken, a refusal naming both when neither is free); src/git/index.ts gained listRemotes and resolveTagCommit; create.ts passes --remote to gh, skips the commit when the index already matches HEAD, tolerates a v0.1.0 tag that points at HEAD, and checks git init. The reported failure was reproduced first with a faithful gh stub: 'Failed to create GitHub repo: X Unable to add remote "origin"'. The fix was verified on the real CLI: a repository with an existing origin published to github with origin left on its original URL, a failed publish retried successfully, both remote names taken refused the publish before any commit, and a v0.1.0 tag on an unrelated commit refused it before a remote was added. test/create.test.ts covers the publish and the retry, including the retry when the repository holds untracked files, which is the case where git uses a different wording for an empty commit. A tag left by an earlier create run moves to the commit this run made, because kitcrate recognises its own collection commits by their subject; a tag kitcrate did not make is left alone and the publish stops.

features.name: Validate a collection that references its own directory
features.description: kitcrate validate warns on a collection whose skill source is '.', which is what kitcrate create writes, because the resolver does not accept a bare '.' as a local path and the source is not resolved relative to the collection.json

features.name: List skills, not collections
features.description: kitcrate list showed every skill twice, once with the collection repo as its source and once with the skill's own repo, and it printed the collection's ref, commit, manifest hash and only filter. The listing is now one entry per skill, with its path, its agents, its collection and its own source, coloured, with a loading spinner for a slow read
features.evidence: pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm test (125 passed, 11 files) and pnpm build all pass. Verified on the real artifact in a pty: one entry per skill, no ref/commit/manifestHash/only, the home directory abbreviated to ~, five agent names then '+N more', bold names with dim paths and labels, a cyan collection and a green source, and the spinner erased before the listing. The JSON lists each skill once with its agent ids and carries no escape sequences. A global skill sharing a name with a project member no longer leaks into the project listing, which was the double listing the user reported

features.name: Install each member skill from its own source
features.description: A collection manifest names where each member skill comes from, with its own ref. kitcrate create writes that owner/repo, add/install/update install each member from it, and kitcrate list shows it, instead of treating every member as living in the collection's repo
features.evidence: pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm test (153 passed, 14 files) and pnpm build all pass. src/core/source.ts parses owner/repo, github:owner/repo, https/ssh GitHub URLs, and a trailing @ref, and returns null or the source unchanged for a local path or another host. src/core/members.ts groups a manifest's members by source and ref, mapping '.' to the collection's own source and ref. src/core/install-members.ts is the one installer add, install and update call. src/commands/progress.ts holds the delayed spinner both list and create use. Overflowing the source parser past 80 columns was caught by pnpm lint against the real file. Verified on the built CLI: a project whose collection entry is github:matt711/mywebskills and whose skills-lock.json records aave/skills renders 'Collection: matt711/mywebskills' and 'Source: aave/skills', while --json keeps both raw. create was run for real against this machine and wrote source aave/skills for account-activity, parsed from the recorded clone URL. test/members.test.ts covers same-source collapsing, different repos, '.' and a member's own ref; test/source.test.ts covers every form; test/create.test.ts covers owner/repo and the '.' fallback; test/add.test.ts records the skills install calls and proves a member asks for its own repo, that two members from one repo share a call, and that a member's ref is carried The source lookup prefers an attributed copy over one with no source of its own, so a skill that sits in both scopes still names the repository it came from, and the collection's own source is passed to the installer in its normalized form, without the ref the user wrote after it, because the skills package reads a trailing @name as a skill filter

features.name: Publish a change to an existing collection
features.description: kitcrate create publishes a collection that does not exist yet. There was no way to push a change to one that already exists: adding a skill to a collection meant editing its repository by hand. kitcrate publish asks which collection to publish, lists the skills that are not in it yet, lets the user pick which to add, copies those skills into the collection's repository along with any local changes to the members it already has, and pushes. A collection the user cannot push to is published to a new repository under their own account
features.evidence: pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm test (202 passed, 18 files) and pnpm build all pass. src/core/publish-targets.ts gathers the candidates: every collection in the project's kitcrate-lock.json, each with its scope, plus every repository among the globally installed skills, de-duplicated across the two forms of one source. src/core/publish-plan.ts holds the pure logic: the folder diff, the member folder lookup by SKILL.md name, the parent directory a new member goes in, the patch bump, and the manifest rewrite. src/commands/publish.ts does the rest: it clones the collection into a temporary directory, never the user's working tree, surveys the installed skills, asks which new ones to add with the same picker create uses, copies them in, rewrites collection.json, bumps the version, commits, tags, and pushes. src/core/release.ts now holds the release tag rule both create and publish use, and src/core/secrets.ts holds the credential exclusion both run. Verified on the real artifact: a local bare repository standing in for GitHub received the new commit, the new member, the updated member, the bumped manifest and the v0.1.1 tag; with push permission refused, a new private repository was created under the user's account and the original repository was left untouched; driven through a real terminal, the collection picker offered both collections with their scope and the skill picker showed an empty box that became a green tick on space. Three defects found in review were fixed: a collection pinned to a tag left the clone detached and the push had no branch, a non-interactive run with several collections installed published the first without saying so, and an installed skill with no folder was reported as changed but never copied
